compute.cost_note: cost is the scored task's cost spread across shards and workers; RAID-scale hygiene runs about 1.5 h with 8 workers versus about 13 h direct

do_not_use_when: the manifest is small enough for check_corpus or the direct tool (sharding adds state and setup overhead)
you cannot keep a persistent --base-dir for state.json between sessions

examples.description: Shard a large manifest for the corpus hygiene task
Work the shards with eight workers

optional: optional flags --task (shard defaults to calibration_survey), --base-dir, --shard-size, --shard-count, --stratify, --shuffle-seed, --workers, --time-window, --fpr-target, --no-sync-state (see each subcommand's --help)
required: subcommand (shard, work, aggregate, status, verify, pause-all, terminate-all, kill-all, sweep-stale, resolve-conflict)
inputs.target: a source JSONL manifest and a base directory for shard state

artifacts: shard files and state.json under the base directory

purpose: Sharded orchestrator for corpus-scale runs. Splits a source manifest into deterministic stratified shards, runs claim/score/done workers (optionally concurrent and time-windowed) with SIGTERM-safe checkpointing in state.json, aggregates results, and supports multi-machine runs through a git-synced state file. Registered tasks include corpus_hygiene (check_corpus at RAID scale) and calibration_survey.
use_when: the corpus hygiene check must run over a manifest beyond about 1M files (check_corpus warns at that size)
a long calibration run needs checkpointing, several workers, or several machines
